title: Normalized isomorphisms of localized functors
statement: Let R,S be commutative rings, C an R-linear preadditive category, D an S-linear preadditive category [def-weil-linear-category], t in R, b in S, and c:R[1/t] → S[1/b] any function. Let U,V:C → D be functors and e:U ≅ V. Let F,G:L_t(C) → L_b(D) be additive functors on raw scalar localizations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], with prescribed object equalities F(K)=U(K), G(K)=V(K). Assume for every integral arrow a and z in R[1/t] that F(z tensor a)=c(z) tensor U(a) and G(z tensor a)=c(z) tensor V(a), interpreted as heterogeneous equalities. Then there exists a unique natural isomorphism alpha:F ≅ G such that alpha_K is heterogeneously equal to Q_D(e_K) for every K. No algebraic laws for c are required beyond the displayed functor map hypotheses.

source.place: Tags 00CV (tensor products), 00CX (universal property), applied to the rational-operation formulas in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom: Common-stage paragraph, rationalization of the scalar-extension comparison theta; naturality of the localized comparison

proof.text: Conjugate the localized integral comparison by the prescribed object equalities. On a pure tensor, the two map formulas and the integral naturality square prove naturality; additivity proves it on zero and sums. The conjugated components are isomorphisms, hence form a natural isomorphism. The prescribed component equality and natural transformation extensionality prove uniqueness.

theorem iso_existsUnique
    {R : Type r} [CommRing R] {S : Type s} [CommRing S]
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C] [Linear R C]
    {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [Linear S D]
    (t : R) (b : S) (c : Localization.Away t → Localization.Away b)
    (U V : C ⥤ D) (e : U ≅ V)
    (F G : ScalarLocalization R C t ⥤ ScalarLocalization S D b)
    [F.Additive] [G.Additive]
    (hF : ∀ K, F.obj K = ⟨U.obj K.obj⟩)
    (hG : ∀ K, G.obj K = ⟨V.obj K.obj⟩)
    (mF : ∀ (K L : C) (a : K ⟶ L) (z : Localization.Away t),
      HEq (F.map (z ⊗ₜ[R] a : ScalarLocalization.mk K ⟶ ScalarLocalization.mk L))
        (c z ⊗ₜ[S] U.map a))
    (mG : ∀ (K L : C) (a : K ⟶ L) (z : Localization.Away t),
      HEq (G.map (z ⊗ₜ[R] a : ScalarLocalization.mk K ⟶ ScalarLocalization.mk L))
        (c z ⊗ₜ[S] V.map a)) :
    ∃! α : F ≅ G, ∀ K, HEq (α.hom.app K)
      ((ScalarLocalization.localization S D b).map (e.hom.app K.obj))
